newsitem.title: USA: Dole sees no role on Medicare commission.
newsitem.headline: Dole sees no role on Medicare commission.

text.p: Former Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole said on Thursday he would turn President Bill Clinton down if he was asked to head a special commission aimed at preserving the Medicare health care system for the elderly.

He was asked whether he would take the job as chairman of a bipartisan commission to make sure the Medicare insurance fund does not go broke in a few years. There has been speculation Clinton might name him to head such a group.

"No, that would be pretty hard to do after he beat us up on it, he distorted the facts. I wouldn't feel right about trying to bail him out," he said in response to a reporter's question outside his Watergate apartment complex.

During the campaign Dole repeatedly accused Clinton of trying to scare senior citizens with ads saying Republicans wanted to cut the Medicare programme, which Dole and other Republicans said was a distortion of the Republican plan to save the system, a plan similar to Clinton's own plan.
Dole was just another man without a job or title on Thursday.

He left his Watergate apartment complex in the morning with a bundle of clothes under his arm and took them to the dry cleaners across the street, like other residents in the Foggy Bottom area of Washington.

The former senator, who had been surrounded by staff for most of his political life during 35 years in Washington, then bought a couple of coffees at a nearby restaurant and gave one to his wife, Elizabeth. Then the couple walked their miniature schnauzer dog, Leader, around the neighbourhood.
Dole was driven off later to have pictures taken with his staff now dismantling his campaign headquarters across town.
